[[Louis Claude Richard|Rich.]] | subdivision_ranks = Species | subdivision = * ''[[Taxodium ascendens|T. ascendens]]'' * ''[[Taxodium distichum|T. distichum]]'' * †''[[Taxodium dubium|T. dubium]]'' * ''[[Taxodium mucronatum|T. mucronatum]]'' |synonyms = * ''Schubertia'' de Mirbel 1812 non Mart. 1824 non Blume 1826 * ''Cuprespinnata'' Nelson }} '''''Taxodium''''' {{IPAc-en|t|æ|k|ˈ|s|oʊ|d|i|ə|m}}''Sunset Western Garden Book,'' 1995:606–607 is a [[genus]] of one to three [[species]] (depending on [[Taxonomy (biology)|taxonomic]] opinion) of extremely [[flood]]-tolerant [[conifer]]s in the cypress family, [[Cupressaceae]]. The name is derived from the [[Latin]] word ''taxus'' '[[Taxus|yew]]' and the [[Greek language|Greek]] word ''εἶδος'' (''eidos'') 'similar to'.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KeGzp-YXrPYC |title=The New York Botanical Garden Illustrated Encyclopedia of Horticulture |volume=10 |first=Thomas H. |last=Everett |publisher=Taylor & Francis |year=1982 |isbn=978-0-8240-7240-7 |page=3299}} Within the family, ''Taxodium'' is most closely related to [[Glyptostrobus|Chinese swamp cypress]] (''Glyptostrobus pensilis'') and [[Cryptomeria|sugi]] (''Cryptomeria japonica''). Species of ''Taxodium'' occur in the southern part of the [[North America]]n continent and are [[deciduous]] in the north and semi-evergreen to [[evergreen]] in the south. They are large [[tree]]s, reaching {{convert|100-150|ft|m|abbr=on}} tall and {{convert|2-3|m|ft|abbr=on|order=flip|round=0.5}} (exceptionally {{convert|11|m|ft|abbr=on|disp=or|order=flip}}) trunk diameter. The needle-like [[leaf|leaves]], {{convert|0.5-2|cm|in|abbr=on|order=flip|1}} long, are borne spirally on the [[Shoot (botany)|shoot]]s, twisted at the base so as to appear in two flat rows on either side of the shoot. The [[conifer cone|cones]] are globose, {{convert|2-3.5|cm|in|abbr=on|order=flip|1}} diameter, with 10–25 scales, each scale with one or two [[seed]]s; they are mature in 7–9 months after [[pollination]], when they disintegrate to release the seeds. The male ([[pollen]]) cones are produced in pendulous [[raceme]]s, and shed their pollen in early spring. ''Taxodium'' species grow [[cypress knees]], when growing in or beside water. The function of these knees is currently a subject of ongoing research. == Species == The three extant [[taxon|taxa]] of ''Taxodium'' are treated here as distinct species, though some [[botanist]]s treat them in just one or two species, with the others considered as varieties of the first described. The three are distinct in [[ecology]], growing in different environments, but [[Hybrid (biology)|hybridise]] where they meet. {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! Image !! Name !! Common name!! (as ''T. sempervirens'' D.Don){{cite web |url=http://www.ars-grin.gov/cgi-bin/npgs/html/splist.pl?11899 |title=GRIN Species Records of ''Taxodium'' |work=Germplasm Resources Information Network |publisher=United States Department of Agriculture |access-date=2010-11-30}} == Uses == [[File:Cypress knee 6016.JPG|thumb|left|[[Cypress knee]]s at low water, Wee Tee Lake, South Carolina]] The trees are especially prized for their [[wood]], of which the [[Wood#Heartwood and sapwood|heartwood]] is extremely [[Decomposition|rot]]- and [[termite]]-resistant. The heartwood contains a [[sesquiterpene]] called cypressene,{{cite journal |url=http://smartech.gatech.edu/dspace/bitstream/1853/1291/1/2077_002_1969.pdf |first=M. A. |last=Buchanan |title=The Fatty Materials in Southern Cypress Wood |date=1965-10-07 |publisher=Institute of Paper Chemistry |page=3 |access-date=2009-10-11 |archive-date=2011-07-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718173145/http://smartech.gatech.edu/dspace/bitstream/1853/1291/1/2077_002_1969.pdf |url-status=dead }} which acts as a natural [[Wood preservation|preservative]]. It takes decades for cypressene to accumulate in the wood, so lumber taken from [[Old-growth forest|old-growth trees]] is more rot resistant than that from second-growth trees.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qOq5v4fd1kcC |title=Native trees for North American landscapes: from the Atlantic to the Rockies |first=Guy |last=Sternberg |author-link=Guy Sternberg |author2=James Wesley Wilson |publisher=Timber Press |isbn=978-0-88192-607-1 |year=2004 |page=476}} However, age also increases susceptibility to Pecky Rot fungus (''[[Stereum]] [[Stereum taxodii|taxodii]]''), which attacks the heartwood and causes some damaged trees to become hollow and thus useless for timber. Bald Cypress wood was much used in former days in the southeastern United States for [[roof shingle]]s.{{Silvics |volume=1 |genus=Taxodium |species=distichum |first1=L. P. |last2=Wilhite |first2=J. R. |last=Toliver |access-date=2009-10-11}} The shredded [[Bark (botany)|bark]] of these trees is used as a [[mulch]]. == Evolution == [[File:Fossil-leaf Taxodium dubium Tertiary Germany.jpg|thumb|left|153px|Fossil leaf of ''Taxodium dubium'', 8 Mil. years old, Hambach lignite open pit mine, Germany]] In earth's history ''Taxodium'' was much more widespread in the Northern Hemisphere than today.{{cite journal |author1=McNair, D.M. |author2=D.Z. Stults |author3=B. Axsmith |author4=M.H. Alford |author5=J.E. Starnes |title=Preliminary investigation of a diverse megafossil floral assemblage from the middle Miocene of southern Mississippi, USA |journal=[[Palaeontologia Electronica]] |date=2019 |volume=22 |issue=2 |page=906 |doi=10.26879/906 |url=https://palaeo-electronica.org/content/pdfs/906.pdf|doi-access=free |bibcode=2019PalEl..22..906M }} The oldest fossils were found in [[Late Cretaceous]] deposits from North America and Asia.{{Cite journal |last1=Kalandadze |first1=N. N. |last2=Kurzanov |first2=S. M. |date=1974 |title=Nizhnemelove mestonakhozhdeniya nazemnykh pozvonochnykh Mongolii [Lower Cretaceous terrestrial vertebrate localities of Mongolia] |journal=Mesozoic and Cenozoic Faunas and Biostratigraphy of Mongolia.}} The trees persisted in Europe until around 2.5 million years ago, during the [[Pliocene]].{{cite book |first=James E. |last=Eckenwalder |title=Conifers of the World |date=14 November 2009 |publisher=Timber Press |isbn=978-0-88192-974-4 |page=591}} ==See also== *[[Bükkábrány mummified forest]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category}} {{Wikispecies}} *[https://www.conifers.org/cu/tax/index.html Gymnosperm Database - Taxodium] *[https://www.audubon.org/local/sanctuary/corkscrew/ Corkscrew Swamp Sanctuary website] *National Audubon Society, undated.
